subject: science
intro: Many materials we use are synthetic, meaning they are made by people through chemical processes, not found ready-made in nature. However, synthetic materials still come from natural resources. For example, plastics are made from petroleum (oil), and many medicines come from processing chemicals found in plants or minerals. Synthetic materials impact society in positive ways (useful products, medicines) and sometimes negative ways (pollution, waste). Understanding their source helps us use resources wisely.

items.prompt: Plastic is a synthetic material. What natural resource is it mostly made from?

steps: Synthetic materials are made from natural resources.
Most plastics are made by processing petroleum.
Petroleum (oil) comes from the ground, a natural resource.

items.prompt: Give one positive and one negative impact of synthetic materials on society.

steps: Positive: synthetic materials provide useful products and medicines.
Negative: some create pollution or waste that is hard to break down.
So they have both benefits and drawbacks.
solution.answer: Positive: useful products/medicines; negative: pollution or waste.

items.prompt: Why is it accurate to say even human-made materials depend on nature?

steps: Synthetic materials are produced by chemical processes.
Those processes start with raw materials taken from nature.
So even human-made materials depend on natural resources.
solution.answer: Because they are made from natural resources taken from the Earth.

steps: Synthetic means made by people through chemical processes, not found ready-made in nature.
solution.answer: Made by people, not found ready-made in nature.

items.prompt: Name one synthetic material and its natural source.
Name one negative impact of synthetic materials.

steps: Synthetic materials can cause pollution or waste.
